title: 4GE1-style exam questions: urbanisation trends and megacities (Paper 2, Topic 6.1)
subject: Geography
source: Seeded from geography/y11 lesson 27 (Own 4GE1-style exam questions with indicative mark points (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 27: Revision: urbanisation trends and megacities (Paper 2, Topic 6.1). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: 'Explain the problems caused by rapid urbanisation.' Portal response box. Use a named city.
questions.a: Congestion and transport, lack of housing (squatter settlements), unemployment and informal work, crime, pollution and waste; each explained with a named example
questions.model: Teacher plans: P1 housing shortage leads to squatter settlements; P2 transport and congestion; P3 environment: waste, air and water pollution; use one named city throughout.

questions.q: Compare urban trends in a developed and a developing or emerging country.
questions.a: Developed: slow growth, suburbanisation and counter-urbanisation; developing: rapid growth from migration and natural increase; comparison words

questions.q: Why might counter-urbanisation create problems in rural areas?
questions.a: House prices rise, pricing out locals (1); villages become commuter areas with fewer services used in the day (1)

questions.q: Explain two reasons for rapid urbanisation in developing countries.
questions.a: Rural-urban migration (1) because of push factors like few rural jobs and pull factors like urban work (1); natural increase (1) because many migrants are young, so birth rates are high (1)
questions.model: Reason 1: migration. Explain it with push and pull. Reason 2: natural increase. Explain: young migrants have children. Two reasons, each developed.

questions.a: Movement of people from the inner city to the edges of the city
People moving back into city centres
options: People moving back into city centres

questions.q: Big question: why are cities in some countries growing much faster than others?
questions.a: Developing countries have strong rural-urban migration and high natural increase; developed countries are already highly urban
